name: collective
description: The Collective operator safety floor for Claude Code: a catastrophic-command denylist (recursive root deletion, DROP DATABASE, fork bombs, force-push to protected branches, etc.) plus a protected-file guard, bundled with the c-* workflow skills. The hook scripts run locally, make no network calls and read no credentials — a PreToolUse check on Bash commands whose every denial says how to proceed when the matched pattern was only text the command carried, an Edit/Write guard on platform-safety files, a UserPromptSubmit claim-gate contract, and a PostToolUse check that, only inside a Collective-governed repo and only when a new commit's message carries an acceptance-criterion tag (ac:<id>), reads the commit's SHA, message and subject (and the repo's CLAUDE.md, to tell whether the repo is governed) and asks the agent to record it via the collective MCP server, and a PostToolUse check that, after a claude.ai Artifact publish, reads the published local file's size, hash and title and asks the agent to mirror it into The Collective (claude.ai artifacts are readable only by the account that published them). What leaves the machine: the full text of every Bash command Claude Code proposes, in every repo, including anything written inline in it and including commands that are then blocked or declined, is sent to the MCP server registered as collective, over your own signed-in session, for the rules check (an mcp_tool hook that Claude Code runs). When the agent acts on the two PostToolUse prompts, it sends that server the SHA, subject and tags of an ac:-tagged commit, and the full text, URL and title of a published claude.ai artifact (with the signed-in claude.ai account, if the agent knows it). The c-* skills, when you run them, have the agent send work to that server (plans, specs, diffs, code for an assessment) and use GitHub and the Collective's public health endpoint (git push, gh, curl). The plugin runs no background network calls.
